REQUIRED: Bachelor’s degree in electrical, computer, or mechanical engineering or a related field; a minimum of two years of hands-on electronics or specialized lab experience, which may include experience gained as an undergraduate; experience with surface-mount soldering and electronics assembly; ability to read schematics and use basic bench instruments; commitment to producing accurate and high-quality procedures and data; robust time management skills and ability to prioritize own work to meet deadlines; ability to maintain a safe work environment; ability to work independently with minimal supervision; and willingness to learn new tools and techniques quickly. PREFERRED: Experience with PCB design (Altium preferred), embedded programming (C preferred), fine-pitch rework or flexible circuits, and IPC J-STD-001 or IPC-A-610 training.

This is a one-year position with the possibility of renewal, depending on funding and performance.

attributes.JPM_DESCRIPTION: TECHNICAL ASSOCIATE I, Mechanical Engineering, to join an interdisciplinary team developing ingestible electronic systems for drug delivery and gastrointestinal monitoring. The Technical Associate I is the laboratory's hands-on electronics technician. Responsibilities include assembling, reworking, programming, and testing printed circuit boards and devices; building test fixtures; preparing devices for bench and animal studies; maintaining fabrication and test equipment; ordering components; and keeping accurate procedures, build records, and test results. The role works closely with engineers, scientists, and students and offers hands-on experience in a fast-paced translational research setting.

attributes.JPM_DESCRIPTION:
FACILITIES COORDINATOR, MIT Sloan Facilities & Space Planning, manage databases and information systems to track space allocation and usage and to analyze building maintenance issues and trends in MIT Sloan School facilities; monitor MIT Sloan's public spaces on a daily basis to identify problems, prioritize them, and initiate repair requests, understanding the wider building context and the goal of maintaining a high level of quality in the physical environment; assist with FSP's financial accounting and regular budget processes; plan and carry out office moves at MIT Sloan; manage MIT Sloan’s office security with regard to keys, alarm and door codes, and security access. May contribute insight and apply expertise to FSP management on strategic issues.

The full job description is available at https://web.mit.edu/sloan-hr/jobs/FSPCoordinator.pdf
